programme.title: Gordon Ramsay's Road Trip
programme.desc: Gino & Fred are excited to head to San Francisco for their very own Summer of Love. Gordon tries to embrace the flower power mood, but he's more interested in the 61 Michelin Stars. The boys travel to a Napa Valley vineyard in a hot air balloon.

programme.title: Gordon Ramsay's Road Trip
programme.desc: After four weeks on the road, Gino's airing his feet in the back seat as the guys cruise along a Texan highway. Texas is a meat lover's paradise, and Gordon is keen to show the Europhiles some of the best BBQ known to man.

programme.title: Gordon Ramsay's Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Mamma Mia! Off We Go Again
programme.desc: Gordon, Gino and Fred travel to Greece to immerse themselves in the culinary traditions. The taste buddies go island-hopping, keen to learn more about the Mediterranean diet and how the country has one of the healthiest populations in the world.

programme.title: Gordon Ramsay's Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Go Greek! Clash of the Titans
programme.desc: The boys are in the Greek capital Athens in a vintage VW campervan. This is where high-concept cuisine originated and is still being re-invented, in a city known as the birthplace of democracy and the cradle of western civilisation.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's India
programme.sub-title: Exploring the Night Markets of Bangalore
programme.desc: Luke heads to the city of Bangalore in southern India; he visits MTR, one of the oldest coffee houses in the city; he learns how to make idli; he meets up with a friend to explore the night markets.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's India
programme.desc: Luke learns about Kongunadu cuisine in Coimbatore, partners with a family in Thrissur to create an authentic delicacy and learns about India's rich coffee culture.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's India
programme.desc: Luke visits the port city of Kochi, Kerala, where he checks out the iconic Chinese fishing nets, does laundry the old-fashioned way and cooks a famous dish. He leaves the city to witness the state's backwaters and local fishing techniques.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's India
programme.sub-title: Hunting for Ancient Spices in Thekkady
programme.desc: Luke visits the lush plantations of spices in Thekkady and then tours Madurai, the spiritual heart of Tamil Nadu, to find hidden gems with the help of a local food journalist.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's India
programme.sub-title: The Outrageous Street Food of Pondicherry
programme.desc: Luke uncovers the history of Chettinad and savours its famous cuisine. He then tastes the chutneys in Kumbakonam and explores the exciting food scene in Pondicherry.

programme.title: Luke Nguyen's India
programme.desc: Luke visits Chennai, the capital of Tamil Nadu, a bustling city with historic ancient temples, and a vibrant modern art scene.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie visits Basilicata in search of some old school Italian recipes and meets a family of shepherds and an 89-year-old macaroni master.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie gets a masterclass in Sicilian sweets and cooking up an epic tuna, prawn and pistachio spaghetti. There's also some chocolaty cannoli.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie tracks down some fast, fresh and easy recipes, featuring tasty minty pea tortiglioni and gnocchi with roasted tomato sauce and rocket pesto.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.sub-title: Best of Salina's Land and Sea
programme.desc: Jamie returns to cooking the food he loves the most, getting right to heart of the Italian kitchen.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie heads for one of the hottest food destinations in Italy, making hand-crafted pasta, a special seafood stew, and the region's answer to paella.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie is taking spaghetti bolognese to the next level and re-creating a mind-blowing Jewish-Italian recipe. There's also beef stew with pappardelle.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie is high up in the Italian Alps cooking some great comfort food, including dumplings, mind-blowing macaroni cheese, and a classic red wine and sausage risotto.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks Italy
programme.desc: Jamie visits the pizza capital of Italy to learn recipes from the locals and tries acquapazza, fish poached in crazy water.

programme.title: The Pizza City You've Never Heard Of
programme.desc: Disturbed by the fact that his hometown of Windsor, Ontario is typically overlooked on lists of the top pizza cities in the world, George Kalivas goes on a mission to set the record straight about where to find the best pies on the planet.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Jamie heads to Greece, to the island of Skopelos, starting on the mainland in Thessaloniki. Inspired by meze plates and traditional island cuisine he cooks up a smoky aubergine flatbread and a lemony chargrilled chicken with tzatziki and rice.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Jamie explores Tunisia to meet traditional couscous makers, eat delicious street food, and get invited to cook with local chefs on a beach. Inspired by everything he sees, Jamie cooks crispy prawn parcels and a chicken and merguez sausage stew.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Jamie heads to Marseille in the south of France. Inspired by their stunning seafood, the traditional flavors of Provence, and the multicultural dishes being served up there, he cooks up a steak with a twist and a sublime courgette and olive tart.

programme.title: Jamie Oliver Cooks the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Jamie's soaking up inspiration in Spain with tapas, flavor-charged rice dishes, and spectacular seafood. He cooks a stunning pork chop with peppers and aioli and a surf and turf skewer of prawns, mushrooms, and local ham.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.desc: The course begins by addressing some of the basic facts about the New Testament; which books it contains, when they are written, in what language and by whom.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.desc: The Epistles of Paul are the earliest books of the New Testament, predating even the Gospels; the realities of writing a letter in the ancient world; issues that affect how one understands Paul's Epistles and the other writings of the New Testament.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.desc: This lecture looks at some of the major teachings of Paul's Epistles; showing how he shapes his theological and ethical views in light of the problems that emerge in his burgeoning Christian communities.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.desc: This lecture considers the broad problem of pseudonymity, or forgery, in the ancient world; applying one's findings to the Pauline letters of the New Testament to see if any, in fact, are written by Paul's followers rather than Paul himself.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.sub-title: The Beginnings of the Gospel Traditions
programme.desc: This lecture looks at the roots of the Gospel narratives in the oral traditions that are spread throughout the Mediterranean in the years after Jesus' death; how they might be modified; what one can know about their historical accuracy.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.desc: The Gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John; what sources of information are available to their anonymous authors; their overarching messages, possible discrepancies among these accounts; whether they can be trusted as reliable historical documents.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.desc: There are many additional accounts of Jesus' words, deeds, death and resurrection that are not included in the New Testament; discussing the reasons why they are excluded; examining two of the most important of them in greater detail.

programme.title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
programme.sub-title: Apocalypticism and the Apocalypse of John
programme.desc: This lecture examines the Apocalypse of John, otherwise known as the Book of Revelation; explaining the religious view known as apocalypticism; the way the book's symbolic descriptions would be understood in the context of the times.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.desc: Professor Koester introduces one of the most discussed books of all time; the Book of Revelation, also known as the Apocalypse; the original meaning of apocalypse; the importance of the apocalyptic tradition; the three-part structure of the course.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.desc: The world of the Hebrew prophets, whose writings deeply influence the author of the Apocalypse; the themes of evil and hope in such works as Ezekiel and Isaiah; how these themes are taken up in the Dead Sea Scrolls and the apocalyptic book of Daniel.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.desc: The apocalyptic worldview, with its sense of conflicting powers, is transformed by Christian writers in the New Testament; apocalyptic themes have a primary place in the early church; the religious matrix out of which the book of Revelation arises.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.sub-title: Origins of the Book of Revelation
programme.desc: A close study of the text of the Apocalypse; looking behind the legends to surmise what can be said about its origins and author, identified only as John; examining the peculiar quality of John's Greek, which is not apparent in most translations.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.desc: The first two chapters of Revelation discuss the issues of the Christian communities that first receive the book; the experiences of the men and women addressed by John; the nature of the persecution and other problems; who this book is written for.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.sub-title: God, the Lamb, and the Seven Seals
programme.desc: John's distinctive images; his word pictures have captured the imaginations of readers for centuries; plunging into some of John's most vivid scenes; the breaking of the seven seals, which unleashes the four horsemen and other startling visions.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.desc: The middle section of the Apocalypse from two perspectives; the futurist view that Revelation is a book of ominous predictions; the literary view that seeks to understand how John organizes his details into a narrative that is surprisingly hopeful.

programme.title: The Apocalypse: Controversies and Meaning in Western History
programme.sub-title: The Dragon and the Problem of Evil
programme.desc: Some dramatic scenes in the Apocalypse; dealing with the problem of evil, personified by Satan, the great red dragon; John's account draws on an ancient fascination with stories of good battling evil; he gives a new interpretation to the conflict.
